title: Doc service crashes on upload when CIFS mount is down (async multer destination)
description: Async multer destination callbacks cause an unhandled promise rejection when fs ops fail (e.g. EHOSTDOWN on the /mnt/cad_iot CIFS mount). title: Privilege escalation: any user can set their own auth_users.is_admin
description:
public.jobcard_is_superuser() reads auth_users.is_admin. The RLS policy auth_users_update_self_or_superuser grants UPDATE to authenticated where id = auth.uid(), with no column restriction. So any signed-in user can run supabase.from('auth_users').update({is_admin:true}).eq('id', <their own id>) from the browser using the anon key and become a superuser.

Fix options: (a) restrict the self-update policy to a column allowlist via a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that reverts is_admin unless the caller is already a superuser or service_role, or (b) drop the broad self-update policy and route legitimate self-writes (e.g. preferred_name) through narrow SECURITY DEFINER RPCs.

Found while adding auth_users.preferred_name (migration 045). Pre-existing, not introduced by that work.

title: Wage sheet dropped hours and re-derived OT instead of using the is_overtime flag

A week of 8h holiday + 32h worked + 6h Sat had the Saturday auto-flagged amber in the grid but paid at basic on the wage sheet.

FIX: the wage sheet now pays on the is_overtime flag - basic unless flagged, uncapped. Flagged hours band by day: Mon-Fri 1.5x, Sat first 5h 1.5x then 2.0x, Sun 2.0x. Holiday counts towards the hurdle, sick does not. The per-project OT breakdown is built from the same numbers as the columns so they cannot disagree. Added a red per-row warning when the rules imply premium hours nobody has flagged against a job.

Rules confirmed by Steve 2026-08-05. Verified with 10 cases incl. hour-conservation (input hours == basic+sick+holiday+x1.5+x2.0). tsc, eslint, next build clean.

title: Portal shows firstname.surname instead of real name
description: auth_users.full_name is built by the public.sync_auth_user_row() trigger, whose coalesce checks raw_user_meta_data->>'name', then given_name/family_name, then falls back to split_part(email,'@',1). title: Sick entries need a reason/exclusion flag for Bradford
description:
SICK-01 carries no reason code, so the Bradford Factor cannot distinguish absence types. The standard legal caution on Bradford is that it must not be applied mechanically: absence related to a disability, pregnancy/maternity, or an industrial injury should normally be discounted from the score or the trigger point adjusted. Under the Equality Act, counting disability-related absence towards a trigger that leads to warnings or dismissal is a well-known route to a discrimination claim - a failure to make reasonable adjustments.

Right now the system cannot support that at all: every SICK-01 day counts identically towards S and D, and there is no way to mark a day as excluded or to record why.

Needs:
- a reason / category on sick entries (self-certified, certified, disability-related, pregnancy-related, industrial injury, other)
- an 'exclude from Bradford' flag, defaulting off, settable by whoever owns absence policy
- calculateBradford to filter excluded dates out of BOTH S and D
- the reports view to show what was excluded, so a suppressed score is visible rather than silent
- consider who is allowed to set the flag - this is sensitive personal data and probably should not be editable by anyone with timesheet access

Blocks using Bradford for anything beyond 'start a conversation'. Raised while reviewing Cywinski, D on 2026-08-05 (platform-portal-b36 session). Pairs with the threshold review.

title: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL baked into prod images points at localhost
description:
scripts/deploy-timed.sh (and deploy.sh) pass NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL from .env.production as a build arg, where it is currently:

  NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://portal.localtest.me:3000

packages/auth/AuthButton.tsx is a client component and reads process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, so Next inlines that value into the client bundle at build time. It is used as the Supabase OAuth redirectTo:

  redirectTo: `${APP_URL}${redirectTo}`

That means production sign-in sends users to http://portal.localtest.me:3000/... — which resolves to the user's own loopback, not the portal. portal.localtest.me is also flagged as a dangerous site by Chrome Safe Browsing.

Pre-existing and identical in every currently-deployed image, so not a regression from platform-portal-b36 — but it looks wrong and nobody has established what it actually breaks in practice (users may simply never hit the sign-in button because sessions persist). Confirm whether prod OAuth works at all, then set .env.production to the real portal origin and rebuild.

Note AuthButton already falls back to window.location.origin when the var is unset, which may be the more robust default for a multi-origin estate.

title: pricing.ts: case-insensitive + whitespace-tolerant grade lookup
description:
Repo: pss-document-service (NOT platform-portal)
File: src/laser/pricing.ts:124-128

Bug: findMaterialGrade() uppercases the input grade then does strict equality against laser_material.grade. If a row stores 'Galvanised' (mixed case) or '5083\n' (whitespace), it never matches. Fall-through path silently returns the class default rate from laser_rate (e.g. rate_mild £950) — pricing wrong but no error.

Proper fix:
1. In findMaterialGrade, compare with .trim().toUpperCase() on both sides:
     materials.find(m => m.grade.trim().toUpperCase() === g)
2. Same for the .includes() loop — normalise m.grade.
3. Consider a DB trigger or app-layer normalisation on insert/update to prevent dirty data recurring (probably better as part of platform-portal-XXX Settings CRUD bead).

Test: add fixture rows with mixed-case/whitespace grades, verify quote pricing picks the row's rate not the class fallback.

title: LaserQuote: material data is split across two unconnected tables
description:
Adding a new material grade requires changes in 3 places that aren't connected:

1. laser_material table (migration 022) — drives ImportForm dropdowns, has its own 'rate' column. NEW grades go here.
2. laser_rate table (migration 021) — key/value rates with hardcoded keys (rate_mild, rate_304, rate_316, rate_al). Drives the Settings page AND the actual pricing lookup.
3. Hardcoded if/else in apps/laserquote/app/imports/[id]/page.tsx:186-193 mapping (material_class, grade) to a laser_rate key.

Symptom: User added laser_material row for MILD/GALVANISED. Row exists, but:
- Doesn't appear in ImportForm pick list (cause TBD — cache or active flag, separate from the architecture issue)
- Doesn't appear in Rates & Settings (by design — Settings only reads hardcoded laser_rate keys)
- Wouldn't price correctly even if selected (pricing if/else has no GALVANISED branch)

The laser_material.rate column appears to be dead data — pricing path never reads it.

Two fix options:
A) MINIMAL: insert rate_galvanised into laser_rate, add GALVANISED branch to pricing if/else, add key to Settings group config. Ships galvanised quickly but perpetuates the dual-table mess.
B) PROPER: finish the migration to data-driven pricing — pricing reads laser_material.rate, Settings page reads laser_material rows, retire laser_rate's rate_* keys (keep burden_rate, density_*, margins, thresholds since those aren't per-grade). Then any new material is one row insert.

title: Timesheets: deactivated employees vanish from history/wages/status panel
description:
When an employee is marked active=false, several display contexts filter them out using .eq('active', true), causing historic data to disappear. Active flag should only gate future entry (the EmployeePicker dropdown), never historic display.

Affected files:
- apps/timesheets/components/EmployeeStatusPanel.tsx:40 — side panel hides deactivated employees even for past weeks where they logged hours
- apps/timesheets/app/reports/page.tsx:155-158, 918 — activeEmployeeCount used as denominator for historic weekly approval ratio (retroactively changes past weeks; can falsely show 'all approved')
- apps/timesheets/app/reports/page.tsx:235-238 — Bradford drops deactivated employees entirely (debatable; needs explicit decision)
- apps/timesheets/app/wages/page.tsx:89 — historic wage prep loses deactivated employees, breaking payroll reconstruction for past weeks

Project hour totals on the report grid are NOT actually missing hours (raw entries query has no active filter at reports/page.tsx:122-130) — but the side panel and wages page drop rows, which feels like missing hours.

Fix approach (Option A, minimal, no schema change):
- Status panel: load all employees, group as 'active no hours / needs approval / approved / inactive (had hours this week)'. Only show inactive when they have entries or approval that week.
- Reports approval denominator: count employees who had any hours that week, not current actives.
- Wages page: include any employee with timesheet entries that week regardless of active.
- Bradford: explicit choice — keep current actives only (label 'Current employees') or include all in window.

EmployeePicker.tsx:24 should keep its active=true filter (correct: gates new entry).
notes: Code changes pushed in commit 0c98c5a. Pending verification on Pi after deploy. Bradford metric still scopes to current actives by design — flag if that needs to change too.

title: Split env into dev (self-hosted Supabase) and prod (cloud); scrub local secrets; de-hardcode pi-deploy.sh
description:
# Why

Wire platform-portal's dev path to the new self-hosted Supabase (http://10.0.0.85:8000)
without risking dev values leaking into production image builds. Also clean up two
working-tree-only secret leaks (service-role key in .env / .env.production.example /
portainer.env) and a soft anon-key hardcode in scripts/pi-deploy.sh.

History review showed the service-role key was NEVER committed (gitignore did its
job — .env.* covers .env.production.example). Anon key is in pi-deploy.sh on main
but is public-safe by Supabase design. So no history rewrite, no force-push.

# What

Env file layout (all in repo root):
- Rename .env -> .env.production (existing real cloud values; gitignored)
- New .env.development (self-hosted Supabase values; gitignored; populated from
  pss-supabase-host/connections.md)
- New env.production.example (committed; placeholders only — note the no-leading-dot
  matches the existing env.example convention since .gitignore has .env.*)
- New env.development.example (committed; placeholders only)
- Keep a copy of .env.production as .env for backward-compat with standalone-app
  pattern (pss-matl-cert and future repos reference ../platform-portal/.env). File
  bd follow-up to migrate standalone repos off this alias.

Selection rules (every consumer is explicit; default is "fail loudly"):
- docker-compose.yml (dev): env_file: .env.development on all 9 services
- scripts/deploy.sh and scripts/deploy-timed.sh: source .env.production; hard-fail
  if missing (no silent fallback to empty NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars)
- scripts/pi-deploy.sh: replace inline hardcoded cloud values with
  source .env.production
- docker-compose.prod.yml / .deploy.yml: no structural change (read shell env at
  compose-eval time); document "source .env.production first" in README
- docker-compose.vm.yml: no change (Portainer injects env at stack level)

Override path (rare — dev against cloud):
- New docker-compose.cloud.yml that flips env_file: .env.production for each service.
  Run with: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.cloud.yml up

Secret scrubbing (working tree only — these files were never committed):
- .env.production: keep real cloud values (it's the canonical for prod builds)
- .env.production.example -> rewrite as committed env.production.example with
  placeholders. Delete the gitignored .env.production.example.
- portainer.env: leave intact (gitignored, used for cloud Portainer stack imports).
  Add a note in docs that this is "cloud" — out of scope for the dev/prod split.

Docs:
- README section: "Dev vs prod env" — which file each path uses, how to flip,
  off-LAN VPN+jump-host caveat for reaching 10.0.0.85 from outside the LAN.
- README section: "Self-hosted dev key rotation" — when pss-supabase-host rotates
  via gen_secrets.py: regenerate connections.md, update .env.development, restart
  dev compose. Cloud rotation is a separate process.
- Update docs/skill_pss_standalone_app.md invariant 4 to reference .env.production
  as the canonical (and note the .env compat alias).

Out of scope (deferred to follow-up issues):
- Cycling the service-role key (deferred per stakeholder; it never hit history)
- Migrating standalone repos off the .env compat alias
- Cleaning the anon key out of historical commits (public-safe; not worth force-push)
acceptance_criteria:
- .env.development exists locally with self-hosted values from connections.md
- .env.production exists locally with the existing cloud values (renamed from .env)
- .env exists as a copy of .env.production (compat alias)
- env.development.example and env.production.example committed with placeholder values
- docker-compose.yml dev services all reference .env.development
- scripts/deploy.sh, deploy-timed.sh, pi-deploy.sh source .env.production and fail
  loudly if missing; pi-deploy.sh no longer hardcodes any values
- docker-compose.cloud.yml exists for the rare dev-against-cloud case
- README documents dev vs prod selection, the override, key rotation, and VPN caveat
- skill_pss_standalone_app.md invariant 4 updated
- bd follow-up issues filed for: standalone-app migration, key rotation

title: Review Bradford thresholds against a year of real scores
description:
The green/amber/red bands in lib/bradford.ts (<50 / 50-199 / 200+) roughly match the widely-cited 51/201/401/601 trigger points, but those are not a standard - CIPD and ACAS mandate no figures, and organisations set their own.

Two reasons our numbers are NOT directly comparable to the published tables:

1. We count Mon-Thu only (Fri/Sat/Sun are elective overtime days). Published trigger points assume a five-day week. Excluding Friday compresses the calendar so a Thursday absence and the following Monday merge into a single spell, suppressing S. Same absences, different S, so the same threshold means something different here.

2. D counts dates, not hours - a 2.5h absence scores the same as a full day. Confirmed intentional by Steve 2026-08-05 ('sick is sick'), but it does inflate D relative to schemes that pro-rata part days.

Now that the rolling 52-week window is in (platform-portal-b36 follow-on), let it run for a full year, then plot where the workforce actually sits and set bands from the real distribution rather than importing numbers built for a different working week.

Reference point: Cywinski, D scored 192 (S=4, D=12) on 2026-08-05 - amber, 8 points under red. Eight of his twelve days were one continuous fortnight, which barely moves the score. Twelve single-day absences would have scored 1728.

title: Reports page ST/OT split disagrees with the wage sheet

- Ignores is_overtime entirely, so it reports OT the wage sheet does not pay and misses manually-flagged OT under 40h.
- Counts HOLIDAY-01 in the total (consistent with the hurdle rule) but so the 'straight' figure mixes worked and holiday hours.

Decide whether this view is meant to mirror payroll or just show hours-over-40 for project reporting. If the former, drive it off is_overtime like the wage sheet. Not urgent - this page is reporting only, no payroll impact.

title: Engineering calculators in the portal, linked from the wiki
description:
Steve wants the engineering reference data on the wiki (Engineering Information shelf: flange tables, metric thread tables, spanner clearance) backed by interactive calculators, hosted in the portal and linked from the wiki pages.

NEEDS PLANNING BEFORE BUILD - scope not yet chosen. See vault note projects/platform-portal/calculators-in-portal.md for the groundwork already done.

Why the portal and not the wiki: BookStack v26.05.2 strips scripts AND form elements by default (content_filtering=jhfa). Verified empirically - a probe page with a script and an input had both removed. Enabling would need ALLOW_CONTENT_SCRIPTS=true (turns off all four filters) or APP_CONTENT_FILTERING=h (granular). Steve chose not to enable it; calculators go in the portal instead. This also matches the existing 'Tools and Calculators' wiki shelf, which is guides to tools that live elsewhere.

PROPOSED SHAPE (not yet agreed):
- A /calculators route INSIDE apps/portal, not a new standalone app. The gateway already routes / to portal, so no new port, container, ghcr image, ARM64 build or nginx change. Inherits @platform/auth and @platform/ui. Calculators are client-side arithmetic with no DB, so a standalone app would be a container for a few forms.
- A 'Calculators' card in the apps array in apps/portal/app/page.tsx.
- Two-way links: wiki reference page -> calculator, calculator -> the page it derives from, carrying the same draft/provenance warning.

KEY OPEN PROBLEM - data drift. The wiki tables are generated from Python tuples in pss-data-wiki/scripts/. Calculators in the portal would be TypeScript. Two repos, two languages, same numbers = they will diverge, especially since three open issues exist to correct that data (pss-data-wiki-2hs, -eqv, -mcd). Proposed fix: the Python build scripts emit a fastener-data.json artifact that both the wiki pages and the calculators read. Needs deciding during planning.

CANDIDATE CALCULATORS (Steve to choose):
- Bolt capacity (tension/shear from stress area x property class) - natural first, both inputs already on the wiki
- Thread / tapping drill lookup
- Flange bolt set picker (standard + DN -> qty, size, length, PCD)
- Steel weight - most used, but needs a section property table the wiki does not have yet
acceptance_criteria: Scope agreed in a planning session; data-sharing approach decided; calculators built, linked both ways with the wiki, and deployed.

title: cookbook gap: docker daemon down — start Docker Desktop + wait for engine

title: Workstation .env.production line 18 breaks 'source' (glued #comment with parens)
description: On the build workstation, .env.production line 18 (DOC_SERVICE_ADMIN_KEY) has an inline '#comment' glued directly to the value with no preceding space, and the comment text contains parentheses. Because there is no space before the '#', it is NOT treated as a shell comment; the '(' then throws 'syntax error near unexpected token (' when the deploy scripts run 'set -a; source .env.production; set +a'. Effect: source aborts at line 18, silently leaving every var AFTER line 18 unset (the DOC_SERVICE_*, MS_*, and NESTING_* runtime vars). Currently harmless for the buildx flow because all 6 NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args are on lines 2-11 (before the error), and runtime vars are sourced from the Pi's own env at container runtime — but it is a landmine: any future build arg placed after line 18 would ship empty. Fix: add a space before the '#' (KEY=val # comment) or move the comment onto its own line, so the parenthetical becomes a real comment. Found while deploying platform-portal-3mf / epic platform-portal-6gr on 2026-07-15.
close_reason: Fixed on the workstation: comment moved to its own line, key value verified byte-identical to backup. Was a hard blocker not a latent one — set -euo pipefail + source exited 2, so deploy-timed.sh died at line 27 before building. Follow-up worth checking separately: whether docker compose was reading the glued '#...' suffix as part of DOC_SERVICE_ADMIN_KEY at runtime.

title: Nesting: portal Rerun loses per-piece member traceability
description:
The portal nesting "Rerun" re-solves from the stored `request_payload`, which is
the consolidated manual-form shape (per-section `{length, qty}` cut rows). That
form has no per-piece member field, so a Rerun produces a cutting list with no
ref_id / member / parent — the member marks are lost.

The Advance Steel BOM → nesting push tool (pss-advancesteel-bom `portal_import`)
submits per-piece items carrying ref_id / member_name / parent, so the *initial*
View cutting list is fully traceable back to BOM member marks (e.g. DB100). But
once a user Reruns in the portal (to tweak stock), traceability is gone.

Options:
1. Widen the portal nesting form + request_payload to carry per-piece member
   marks (member/parent on cut rows) so Rerun preserves them. Touches
   apps/nesting/NestingPage.tsx, the SavedPayload shape, and how items are built.
2. Leave the form as-is and document that a traceable list requires re-pushing
   through the BOM tool rather than using Rerun.

Discovered during the Advance Steel BOM → nesting POC (quotes go to project 0005).
Workaround today: re-push via `bom_poc.portal_import` for a traceable list.

value:
PSS wage/OT rules (confirmed by Steve 2026-08-05, platform-portal-b36, verified live on the Pi). TWO things decide pay and they are NOT the same: (1) timesheet_entries.is_overtime says which JOB the overtime went to; (2) the 40h threshold says HOW MANY hours are actually premium. Do not let the flag decide both — that was the second bug.

RULES: An hour is BASIC unless flagged, and basic is uncapped (never discard hours). Flagged hours must first top basic up to the threshold, EARLIEST ENTRY FIRST, so a flagged entry straddling the threshold splits — only the excess is premium. Rate for the excess depends on the day: Mon-Fri 1.5x, Saturday first 5h 1.5x then 2.0x (the 5h allowance applies to PREMIUM Saturday hours, not all Saturday hours), Sunday 2.0x. HOLIDAY-01 counts towards the threshold; SICK-01 does not. The threshold never gates payment — it only decides which hours SHOULD be flagged; TimesheetGrid auto-flags weekend cells on crossing it and the wage sheet warns on unflagged excess.

CANONICAL CASE (Earnshaw, C week 31): unflagged hours = 38.00, earliest flagged entry = 2.75h on 10370-01 -> 2.00 basic + 0.75 @1.5x, giving Basic 40.00 / x1.5 15.75. Not 38.00 / 17.75.

Always assert HOUR CONSERVATION when changing this: input hours == basic + sick + holiday + x1.5 + x2.0.

Three places implement hours logic: TimesheetGrid.tsx (entry + auto-flag), app/wages/page.tsx (payroll), app/reports/page.tsx (still naive whole-week min(total,40), not reconciled — platform-portal-3a7).

Standalone repo trap (2026-04-20): app/.dockerignore is MANDATORY. Without it, host npm install creates Windows-path symlinks in node_modules for file: deps (@platform/ui/auth/supabase). 'COPY . .' in the builder stage overlays those broken symlinks on top of the container's clean node_modules and the build fails with 'Module not found: Can't resolve @platform/ui'. matl-cert avoided this by chance (no local node_modules existed when first built). Always include .dockerignore that excludes node_modules, .next, .env*, .git.

Portainer-on-VM deploy gotchas (2026-04-30, learned during docker01 first deploy): (1) Disk: needs 50+ GB free (15 GB Ubuntu default fails). (2) platform_net must be created BEFORE deploy and may not survive reboots — add a systemd one-shot to recreate. (3) Re-pull image MUST be unticked in Portainer redeploy for VM path (images are local-only, never pushed) — only Re-build image. Re-pull causes 'pull access denied for platform-portal/<svc>'. (4) NEXT_PUBLIC_* are baked at build time; changing them needs a real rebuild AND removing the old images first ('docker images platform-portal/* -q | xargs docker rmi') because layer cache silently reuses old build layers. (5) HOST_DOC_ROOT must be a Linux path on the VM, never a Windows path copied from dev .env. (6) BuildKit corruption (unpigz crc32 mismatch) after disk-full events: 'docker builder prune -af'. (7) Supabase Auth → Redirect URLs allowlist must include http://<vm-ip>:<port>/** matching NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL exactly (scheme, host, port). (8) If Portainer says 'deployed successfully' but Stacks shows zero containers, the build succeeded but compose up failed silently — most likely platform_net missing.

Centralised .env convention (2026-04-20): platform-portal/.env is canonical for all projects. Siblings reference it via env_file: ../platform-portal/.env in their docker-compose.app.yml. On the Pi, layout is /opt/platform-portal/.env and /opt/pss-<app>/ as siblings. App-specific overrides (PORT, container-name) stay inline in the compose; cross-app secrets/URLs live in the shared file only. Edit secrets in one place.

Extraction rationale (2026-04-20 retro): the original thesis 'extraction cuts build time' was wrong — per-app build cost is dominated by next build and docker push regardless of repo location. Extraction is for LIFECYCLE ISOLATION (independent start/stop/rollback, separate release cadence) not speed. matl-cert was extracted for compliance reasons; pss-assembly-viewer for canary/cutover practice. Don't extract apps that share heavily with portal/jobcards.

Standalone-mode rollout (2026-04-20): BuildKit cache patch eliminated the pnpm install tax (~42s/app saved on incremental). Next.js output: 'standalone' + outputFileTracingRoot dropped runtime image from ~800 MB to ~100 MB and push time from ~38s to ~7s. Total full-sweep time barely moved (~1200s) because next build + push still dominate per-app — that's the floor. The real win is on partial rebuilds (~5s for unchanged apps) and on Pi disk pressure.

Timesheet panel badge discipline (2026-04-29 sv5 retro): EmployeeStatusPanel badges should only surface signals that change which employee the foreman opens next (e.g. Bradford routes attention to absence patterns, hours pill flags zero/low). The variance badge was reverted because it duplicated information already visible in the grid when the employee is opened — adding triage clutter without proportional triage value. Supabase allowlist matcher silently fails for ALL IPv4-literal+port redirect URLs — has been broken from the start, not a regression (2026-04-30, confirmed on docker01 deploy). Symptom: redirect_to=http://<ip>:<port>/ correctly sent in /authorize, but Supabase callback rewrites Location to whatever Site URL is configured as, regardless of whether the requested URL is in the allowlist (even with both /** wildcard AND bare entries). Site URL fallback has been doing 100% of the redirect work for IP+port URLs; allowlist entries with IPv4 literals are decorative. PROOF: flipping Site URL from http://10.0.0.75:3000 to http://10.0.0.95:3000 caused production (.75) traffic to bounce to .95 within seconds — symmetric breakage confirms allowlist match is genuinely failing for both IPs, only Site URL works. DO NOT use the Site URL flip as a workaround — it has full prod blast radius (we briefly broke prod doing exactly this and had to revert immediately). Real workarounds: (a) use a real hostname instead of an IP for non-prod environments — add DNS or /etc/hosts entry, set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://<hostname>:<port>, add http://<hostname>:<port>/** to allowlist; hostnames empirically match where IPs don't. (b) use a separate Supabase project per environment — clean isolation, requires schema duplication. (c) file a Supabase support ticket with HAR/log artefacts; this is their bug. Diagnostic notes: GoTrue auth log 'referer' field is NOT the HTTP Referer header — it's an internal computed value (often Site URL) and reads identically across all requests, so don't rely on it for diagnosis. auth.flow_state table is empty for implicit-grant Azure flow (PKCE only), so server-side state isn't queryable that way. Bake-check command to verify NEXT_PUBLIC_* in a built portal:vm image: docker run --rm platform-portal/portal:vm sh -c 'grep -rohE "localtest|10\.0\.0\.[0-9]+" /repo/apps/portal/.next 2>/dev/null | sort -u'.

Portainer-on-VM deployment disk sizing (2026-04-30, confirmed working): a from-scratch build of platform-portal (9 apps) needs ~50+ GB free at deploy time. 15-20 GB VMs (Ubuntu Server defaults) fail mid-build with 'no space left on device' during layer extraction — Docker images alone hit 3.5 GB and build cache another 2 GB before any pnpm install completes. Steady state after success is ~10-15 GB. Recommended: 60-80 GB total VM disk. If using LVM and the VG has free space (check vgs), claim it with lvextend -l +100%FREE first before resizing the Proxmox virtual disk. After Proxmox resize: growpart /dev/sda 3, pvresize, lvextend, resize2fs. First successful deploy was on docker01 (80 GB).

Two distinct deployment paths for platform-portal (2026-04-29): (1) Pi path uses docker-compose.deploy.yml + scripts/deploy.sh, builds on dev machine, cross-compiles ARM64, distributes via ghcr.io/ukstevem/platform-portal/*, Pi pulls. Documented in docs/portainer-deployment.md. (2) VM path uses docker-compose.vm.yml, Portainer Stack repository mode, clones repo and builds locally on the VM (amd64), images tagged platform-portal/<svc>:vm and never pushed anywhere. Documented in docs/portainer-vm-deployment.md. Do not mix paths on the same host. Same NEXT_PUBLIC_* build args are required for both. The 'don't build on Pi' rule is Pi-specific (slow ARM); building on a reasonable amd64 VM is fine.
